thread:
Anand: Heads-up — partner QA found perf/regressions when we run model on driver 535.12 + CUDA 12.2 on their marketplace image.
Leah: ugh, is this the same perf cliff from last month or a new regression?
Natalie: looks new. They see token-level latency spikes after KV cache hits. Happens on p4d-equivalent instances.
Tom: can you paste the minimal repro logs?
Anand: pasted below — short snippet from partner:```
2026-03-10T14:22:11Z inference: step 1 done, latency=23ms
2026-03-10T14:22:12Z inference: step 2 done, latency=230ms
kv_cache: hit=true, size=1.2MB
```
Leah: that 10x jump lines up with a kernel fallback. Could be a cuBLAS/driver kernel selection change in 535.12.
Sri: cc @partner-bot — can you confirm the marketplace image uses our recommended pinned stack or the partner's custom drivers?
partner-bot: marketplace-ci: image builds show base: ubuntu22.04, cuda:12.2, driver:535.12 (partner-provided), rocm: N/A, runtime: nccl/2.17.
Maya: Marketplace PM here — partner said they pushed a GA image today. We need to decide if we ask them to roll back to 530.x or push a hotfix on our side.
Natalie: rollback is fastest for public-facing customers. But for SI integrations a rollback could break other apps. We need to scope blast radius.
Tom: Ops note — Dedicated pools can be configured with a driver pin override per-customer. We can route affected tenants to pinned 530.41 until triage completes.
Anand: good idea. Can we ship a short canary to 5% of traffic?
Leah: yes — Redwood routing policy supports canary by tag. I'll prepare route change.
Sri: On partner coordination: their engineering lead wants a joint statement if we publicly ask for rollback. They prefer a silent roll forward.
Maya: We also have a marketplace announcement scheduled next week. If we ask for rollback it might delay the launch. Need comms alignment.
Natalie: Proposed plan: (1) immediate canary redirect to 530.x for affected SKUs, (2) partner rolls driver back in marketplace image and re-run QA, (3) our infra team prepares a micro-patch that mitigates kernel fallback (if possible) — if not, we keep pinned until vendor fix.
Tom: I'll open a rollback lane playbook and a one-click pin in the console. ETA 3 hours.
Leah: I'll coordinate with infra on tracing hooks and add perf traces around KV cache paths.
Anand: partner asked about a hotfix timeline. Let's offer two options: rollback now (fast) or joint hotfix with chip vendor (2-3 weeks).
partner-bot: vendor-ticket created: NV-2026-0421, severity=high, linked to partner CI logs.
Maya: For marketplace go-live: suggest we hold public announcement until partner confirms rollback or vendor fix. We can still run private previews.
Sri: Agree. Also flag any SI integrations — I'll ping systems integrators to warn them about the pinned behavior.
Natalie: I'll draft a short customer note: "We detected a performance regression on driver 535.12 with certain marketplace images. We've pinned affected SKUs to a validated driver and are coordinating with partners and the GPU vendor. No action needed by customers unless we ask otherwise."
Anand: write that note and drop it here when ready. I'll sync with partner legal on wording.
Leah: quick ops checklist I'm going to run: `kubectl label nodes canary=true && route set --tag=canary --driver-pin=530.41 --percent=5` — will post the exact commands in #eng-runtime after approvals.
Tom: ping me when you flip the canary, I'll watch infra metrics and be ready to roll back fully.
Maya: I'll postpone the marketplace blog and update product marketing.
partner-bot: partner update: partner will revert marketplace image by EOD and re-run their end-to-end.
Natalie: perfect. Once they confirm, we can expand the rollback to 100% for affected SKUs and resume announce plan.
Anand: thanks all. Next steps captured. Natalie, please post the customer note and I'll loop legal. Leah/Tom/Sri coordinate the canary and partner comms.
Leah: will do — posting the trace instrumentation and command snippets in 20m. :thumbsup:
Tom: monitoring on standby.
Natalie: customer note draft in 10.
partner-bot: incident-log: updated NV-2026-0421 with partner repro and our canary plan.
